gloss: imperial dolls; the emperor and empress pair of a hina display

definitions.gloss: imperial dolls; the emperor and empress pair of a hina display
definitions.explanation: The two dolls placed on the top tier of a {雛人形|ひなにんぎょう} display for the March 3 Doll Festival, dressed as the Heian imperial couple. Sold and spoken of as a pair, and often the only dolls a household displays.

examples.japanese: {内裏雛|だいりびな}を{一番上|いちばんうえ}に{飾|かざ}る。
examples.english: We put the emperor and empress dolls on the top tier.

examples.japanese: {狭|せま}いので{内裏雛|だいりびな}だけ{飾|かざ}っています。
examples.english: Our place is small, so we only display the imperial pair.

examples.japanese: {雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}の{一番|いちばん}{上|うえ}の{段|だん}に{内裏雛|だいりびな}、その{下|した}に{三人官女|さんにんかんじょ}が{並|なら}ぶ。
examples.english: The imperial pair goes on the top tier of the doll display, with the three court ladies on the tier below.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {内裏雛|だいりびな}を{飾|かざ}る: to display the imperial pair
- {内裏雛|だいりびな}を{片付|かたづ}ける: to put the dolls away (traditionally soon after March 3)
- {親王|しんのう}{飾|かざ}り: a display consisting of the imperial pair only

CULTURAL NOTE:
In conversation the two are usually called お{内裏|だいり}{様|さま} (the male doll) and お{雛|ひな}{様|さま} (the female doll). Placement differs by region: in Tokyo-style displays the male doll sits on the viewer's left, in Kyoto-style displays on the right.
